event_headline: Philippine prosecutors present bank testimony and receipts documenting VP Sara Duterte's P125M confidential fund withdrawals including 'Mary Grace Piattos' case

chronology.action: Withdrew and spent P125 million in confidential funds over 11 days, documented through acknowledgment receipts
Testified that OVP's encashment of P125M in confidential funds was 'unusual' despite full procedural compliance with advance notice and withdrawal protocols
Established public source of P612.5M funds through testimony in Sara Duterte's trial
Testified that OVP used confidential funds to purchase P40 million in medicines, explicitly prohibited by auditing rules
Testified that P125M confidential fund liquidation documents systematically marred by irregularities including late-dated receipts and missing supporting documentation
Presented receipts bearing improbable names including 'Mary Grace Piattos,' 'Andy C. Lim,' and 'Patty Ting' as evidence of P125 million confidential fund disbursements
Granted banks additional time to submit VP Duterte's subpoenaed financial documents
Acknowledged the P125 million spending but promised 'an explanation' rather than providing actual documentation
Invoked 1992 COA circular to justify absent receipts for confidential fund expenditures
Labeled VP Duterte's confidential fund usage a 'scam' while examining former COA auditor
Objected to marking Arturo Lascañas's affidavit linking Sara Duterte to extrajudicial killings
Argued no COA regulation prohibits spending P125 million confidential funds in eleven days
Disallowance notices discovered to contain arithmetic errors during impeachment examination

key_actors.role: Subject of impeachment trial regarding confidential fund usage
key_actors.stated_position: Camp acknowledged P125M spending but promised 'an explanation' without providing documentation

key_actors.name: Roderick Wamil
key_actors.stated_position: Testified that OVP used confidential funds for prohibited medicine purchases and that liquidations systematically lacked supporting documentation

key_actors.name: Lorna Kapunan
key_actors.stated_position: Labeled VP Duterte's confidential fund usage a 'scam' and presented receipts with improbable recipient names

factual_claims.claim: OVP withdrew P125 million in confidential funds between December 21-31, 2022
COA auditing rules explicitly prohibit using confidential funds to purchase medicines
Acknowledgment receipts submitted to COA included recipients named 'Mary Grace Piattos,' 'Andy C. Lim,' and 'Patty Ting'
OVP used confidential funds to purchase P40 million in medicines
Sara Duterte was the only vice president and DepEd secretary ever to receive confidential fund appropriations
DepEd did not submit documentation for confidential funds allocated to counter-insurgency programs
DepEd's confidential fund plans for three quarters failed to specify activities to be carried out
A 1992 COA circular exists that defense claims justifies absent receipts for confidential expenditures

verified_facts.claim: Sara Duterte was the only vice president and DepEd secretary ever to receive confidential fund appropriations
verified_facts.finding: Multiple sources confirm that a Commission on Audit (COA) auditor testified that Sara Duterte was the only vice president and DepEd secretary to receive confidential fund appropriations among the past three administrations. The testimony was given by a COA auditor serving as a prosecution witness on Monday, according to consistent reporting across multiple Philippine news outlets.

verified_facts.claim: A 1992 COA circular exists that defense claims justifies absent receipts for confidential expenditures
verified_facts.finding: The search results show that a 1992 COA circular exists (COA Circular No. 92-385) governing confidential funds, and Duterte's defense lawyers invoked it to justify missing receipts in Vice President Sara Duterte's confidential fund spending. Prosecutors countered that stricter 2015 audit rules supersede the 1992 circular.

disputed_claims.claim: Whether the P125M withdrawal was procedurally proper
disputed_claims.competing_accounts: Bank officials testified it was 'unusual' but procedurally compliant with advance notice protocols (J9); Defense argues no COA regulation prohibits spending this amount in eleven days (J48); Prosecution labels it a 'scam' (J44)

disputed_claims.claim: Whether COA auditor testimony confirms violations
disputed_claims.competing_accounts: Prosecution emphasizes systematic irregularities, prohibited medicine purchases, missing documentation (J22); Defense claims auditor's 'no violation' remark exonerates (J46, noting misrepresentation); Actual testimony shows 'no violation' applied narrowly to one document while broader irregularities were flagged (J46)

disputed_claims.claim: Relevance of 1992 COA circular to current case
disputed_claims.competing_accounts: Defense invokes 1992 circular to justify missing receipts (J38); Prosecution challenges its relevance against 2015 regulations (J44)

competing_frames.summary: Confidential funds were systematically misused through prohibited purchases, fabricated recipients with improbable names, missing documentation, and late-dated receipts constituting deliberate fraud
Expenditures followed proper withdrawal protocols, no regulation prohibits the spending timeline, and 1992 COA circular justifies documentation practices
The P125M encashment was unusual in scale and timing but met all advance notice and procedural requirements for withdrawal

Impeachment proceedings produce detailed evidentiary records through livestreamed testimony but may lack enforcement mechanisms to convert documentation into consequences, with procedural objections potentially preventing substantive fraud allegations from triggering criminal prosecution
